To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HyPer can achieve OLTP transaction rates of 100000 per sec and OLAP query execution times in the range of a few seconds on the same system.

HyPer is able to execute a TPC-C benchmark with up to 100000 transactions per second and a TPC-H benchmark with a 1000 times larger database (100GB) with a 100x larger query result set (10GB) on the same machine in parallel.
HyPer is a novel main-memory database system, based on virtual memory, that achieves both OLTP and data warehouse performance at unprecedented levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a new hybrid main memory database system that combines OLTP and OL AP workloads on a single system.
the design and implementation of a hybrid OLTP and OLTP database system.
the design and implementation of an OLTP&OL AP database system that can handle both transactional and analytical workloads on the same system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HyPer is a very fast and efficient hybrid system that combines the best of two worlds.
HyPer is the fastest database system in the world, at least in terms of the combined OLTP/OLAP performance, which is the only meaningful metric for hybrid OLTP& OLAP systems.
HyPer is able to handle both OLTP as well as OLAP queries at the same time, while being more than an order of magnitude faster than a state-of-the-art OLTP-only database system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HyPer is the first database system that combines the two worlds of OLTP and OLTP in a single database and is able to handle the two workloads in a way that both are executed in real time and with very high performance.
HyPer is a hybrid OLTP/OLAP database system that achieves unprecedented high performance for both transaction processing and data analytics on a single system.
HyPer achieves OLTP performance comparable to the fastest in-memory OLTP system and OLAP performance comparable to the best column-store database systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the separation of OLTP and OL AP is not necessary anymore and can be replaced by a hybrid system.
the separation of transactional and analytical data is not necessary anymore and that a single system that combines both worlds is feasible and efficient.
a single main-memory database system can handle OLTP and OLAp simultaneously.
